visa.title: China Visa Guide 2026
visa.desc:
Do you need a visa to travel to China? It depends on your passport, purpose and route.
Check visa-free and transit options first. If a visa is needed, compare China visa types, requirements, documents, fees and processing time before applying.
visa.item1: 10-day visa-free transit — Best for short visits and multi-city stopovers.
visa.item1-desc: Eligible for travelers from the US, UK, Canada and 50+ other countries — ideal for trips connecting through Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou or Shenzhen.
visa.item2: 30-day visa-free entry — Perfect for classic China itineraries
visa.item2-desc: For citizens of Italy, Australia, Spain, Germany, France, New Zealand, Belgium, the UAE and 29+ other states.
visa.item3: Regional visa-free programs — Selected countries and travel periods
visa.item3-desc: Visitors from selected countries in Latin America and the Gulf region may enjoy visa-free stays of up to 30 days during designated periods between 2025 and 2026.

china.card1.title: How to Plan Your First China Trip
china.card1.desc: Before booking attractions, decide on your travel season, trip duration, and route. These six steps will help you create a practical China travel plan and prepare the essentials for your first trip.
china.card2.title: What to Prepare Before Your First China Trip

trip.title: Best Time to Visit China in 2026
trip.subtitle:
China is suitable for travel all year round, but timing is crucial. Summers are hot, humid, and rainy with many tourists;
while winters are better for snow scenery, hot springs, the Harbin Ice Festival, and visiting southern China.
trip.desc1:
Spring is one of the best times to visit China.
Temperatures begin to rise, flowers bloom, and the climate in northern, central, and southern China is generally comfortable.
April and May are particularly good for outdoor activities, city sightseeing, and classic China tours.
The Great Wall, Forbidden City, Guilin, Yangtze River, and Yunnan are excellent choices.

Best for: Blooming flowers, pleasant weather, classic tours
Best destinations: Beijing, Xi'an, Guilin, Yunnan, Yangtze River
trip.desc2:
Many regions in China are hot, humid, rainy, and busy in summer.
July is usually one of the hottest months, with temperatures often around 30°C or higher in major cities.
However, summer is a great time to visit mountains and high-altitude areas. Tibet, Qinghai, Inner Mongolia, Jiuzhaigou, and Western Sichuan offer cool climates and magnificent scenery.

Best for: Mountains, grasslands, family vacations, Tibet travel
Best destinations: Tibet, Jiuzhaigou, Inner Mongolia, Qinghai, Zhangjiajie
trip.desc3:
Autumn is the best season to visit China.
The weather is cool, skies are clear, rainfall is less, and scenery becomes colorful in many places.
It is the ideal time to visit Beijing, Xi'an, Zhangjiajie, Jiuzhaigou, Guilin, and Yunnan.
November is also a good choice with fewer tourists and better prices, especially in southern China. Try to avoid the first week of October due to the National Day Golden Week.

Best for: Clear skies, autumn colors, photography, comfortable sightseeing
Best destinations: Beijing, Great Wall, Jiuzhaigou, Zhangjiajie, Yunnan
trip.desc4:
Northern China is cold in winter, but many southern regions are mild.
In January, temperatures in northern China can drop below -10°C, especially in Harbin and Inner Mongolia.
Winter is the best time to visit the Harbin Ice Festival, experience snow festivals, enjoy hot springs, and travel on a budget. Southern China, Yunnan, and Hainan have milder climates and are ideal for winter travel.

Best for: Harbin Ice Festival, snow scenery, lower prices, fewer tourists
Best destinations: Harbin, Beijing, Yunnan, Hainan, Southern China
